title: Passover: a candle and a feather
hook: the night before, a search for leaven by candlelight

segments.voice: Yesterday, chametz, the leaven cleared from the house. Your line was clear out the puffed-up. Did you say something smaller and truer? Today, the night of the final search. Day six hundred seventy-seven.

It's the night before Passover. The house has been cleaned for weeks. The kitchen is scrubbed; the counters are covered. And now the lights go off. A parent lights a single candle. A child holds a feather and a wooden spoon. Somebody else carries a paper bag. They walk slowly through the dark house, room by room, peering into corners, under the couch, along the windowsills. And here's the funny part: everyone knows what they'll find. Earlier, someone hid a few little pieces of bread around the house, wrapped so they won't leave crumbs. The search is real, and it's also a kind of game.
screen: `THE LIGHTS GO OFF.` → `A CANDLE, A FEATHER, A SPOON.` → `TEN HIDDEN PIECES.`

segments.voice: Bedikat chametz means the search for leaven. The Mishnah opens its tractate on Passover with it: on the night of the fourteenth of Nisan, one searches for chametz by the light of a lamp. Why at night, and why a candle? The Talmud says night is when people are home, and a small flame is better than daylight for this job, because you can carry it into holes and cracks where sunlight never reaches. A torch is too big and scary to bring close. So: one candle, close up. The Talmud also finds verses about searching with lamps. One is from Proverbs, in the old Jewish translation: "The spirit of man is the lamp of the LORD, searching all the inward parts." The rabbis set it beside the night search: a candle moving through the house, and the lamp the proverb says searches a person. The feather sweeps the crumbs into the spoon. The hidden pieces are a later custom, so the search never comes up empty, and so the blessing said before it isn't wasted. When it's done, the family says a short Aramaic declaration: any leaven I haven't seen or found is nullified, ownerless, like the dust of the earth. In the morning, what was collected is burned. Then comes the honest part of the ritual. You searched carefully. You'll still miss something. Jewish law expects that, and the declaration covers it. The search asks for real attention, and then forgives you for being human.
screen: `THE NIGHT OF THE FOURTEENTH.` · `A CANDLE GOES INTO THE CRACKS.` · `THE LAMP OF THE LORD SEARCHES.` · `WHAT YOU MISSED IS LIKE DUST.` · then, large: `SEARCH BY CANDLE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: look for one hidden thing. If you like, light a candle, or just dim the lights. Breathe slowly. Bring your attention close, like a small flame, to one corner of your life you don't usually look at: a habit, a resentment, an unanswered message. Don't fix it yet. Just see it clearly, the way a candle shows a crumb. Then let go of what you can't find tonight. The bell holds the time.
Bedikat chametz. The search for leaven, by candlelight, on the night before Passover. Today's word.
Your line: search by candle. Tonight, before bed, take one small light into one dark corner, of your home or your day, and look. Day six hundred seventy-seven.

howItsDone: On the night before Passover, families say a blessing and search the house for chametz by candlelight, often with a feather and wooden spoon and a few hidden pieces of bread, then recite the Aramaic nullification and burn the chametz the next morning.

notes: Editor review (2026-10-01): "ten pieces" made "a few" (count not in the cited texts; many communities do use ten), and the narrator no longer states that the candle is "the same light God uses"; it is now the rabbis' pairing.
Proverbs 20:27 quoted from JPS 1917 from memory; verify.
Pesachim 7b–8a: candle not torch, not sunlight or moonlight; candle can be brought into holes and cracks; Proverbs 20:27 and Zephaniah 1:12 among the verses. Verify.
Reason for night ('when people are home') is from Pesachim 4a; simplified.
Ten pieces: a later custom (associated with the Ari; mentioned by the Rema). Reasons simplified.
Kol chamira paraphrased; nullification formula differs slightly between the night and the morning.
